source: transpile-and-count on ibm_fez (no QPU), C4929 recount of the depth-blocked list

findings.structural_cheap_reframe_REAL: a [[4,2,2]] logical Bell pair costs 2 physical 2q (CZbar=S^4, the entangling gate is single-qubit) -- Clifford-heavy LOGICAL algorithms on [[4,2,2]] are near-free (why Exp244 landed at 19). Holds within the DETECTION regime.
findings.path1_frame_tracking_OVERSTATED: 'the wall may be an accounting artifact' is FALSE for distance-3 correction. Error-corrected magic = 82 > 54. The 45-gate cost is heavy-hex ROUTING of a co-located transversal CNOT, NOT frame-trackable Clifford gates. My Path-1 claim was the wrong tool.
findings.path2_divide_conquer_VALIDATED: the 82 is routing-dominated: 37 for the two encodes (the logic) + 45 for routing the transversal CNOT across 18 co-located qubits. A DISTRIBUTED nonlocal-CNOT (1 Bell pair + feed-forward, relay-style ~12 gates) replaces the 45-gate tax -> projected ~49 < 54. Error-corrected magic is blocked by ROUTING, not logic -- and divide-and-conquer projects it UNDER the wall.

verdict: the depth wall for error-corrected magic is a ROUTING wall, not a logic wall or an accounting artifact. Path 1 (frame-tracking) does NOT rescue it (honest correction). Path 2 (distribute the gate) projects it to ~49 < 54 -- the concrete next check. Walls-are-ideation-prompts vindicated, via a different lever than first proposed.

distributed_test_c4930.finding: single-chip distribution makes it WORSE (152 > 82): the 9 mediating Bell pairs must each be routed across the same A-B gap -> no free lunch on one chip. My Path-2 ~49 projection was WRONG (2nd honest correction).
distributed_test_c4930.true_verdict: error-corrected magic on two co-located distance-3 blocks is genuinely single-chip ROUTING-limited (82); NEITHER frame-tracking (Path 1) NOR single-chip distribution (Path 2) reduces it. The genuine depth-reducing levers are OFF this chip: (a) a MULTI-chip network with real pre-shared entanglement across links (campaign has two-chip F82); (b) a hardware-native code (surface-code patches, geometric transversal CNOT); or (c) STOP trusting the gate-count heuristic -- the 54 wall was 242 fragile XX leg; the MAGIC witness (X-bar) is byproduct-robust + postselected (243 ran clean at 19), so fly the 82-gate version and TEST whether the robust witness survives, rather than declare it blocked by a count.

topology_study_c4932.finding: the routing wall is a HEAVY-HEX TOPOLOGY artifact, quantified: pure logic = 25 gates; heavy-hex routing -> 82 (over 54 wall); surface-native 2D grid -> 41 (UNDER 54 wall = flyable). Error-corrected magic is not fundamentally depth-blocked -- it is blocked by ibm_fez connectivity. A hardware-native (surface-code / grid) topology dissolves it. The off-chip lever is real and numbered.
